review.method: the acceptance suite run locally with `CS_GAME_DIR` and `CS_ENGINE_IMAGE` set, every `accept_t542_` test selected by prefix with `--include-ignored`; this harness derives every field from the recorded log, production discovery of $CS_GAME_DIR, the eye census the retail test derived over that installation and the mechanism record the image test derived over the owner-supplied decrypted executable, and a second full production re-run of the measured chain inside the harness itself (`decode_interp`, `discover_cockpit_bindings`, `discover_airframe_roster`, `read_gamez_nodes` over `ZBD/planes.zbd`, `audit_cockpit_coverage`, `resolve_cockpit_eye`, `load_engine_image`, `eye_mechanism_source` and the instruction byte pins), which re-derives all eleven airframes' `Declared` eyes — each the `cockpit_camera` node's stored translation triple — and the registration's eight-call target list rather than trusting the log; both artifacts are checked against this report's own tree and hashes before they are referenced, so a stale file cannot be reported as this run's. Validated with tools/validate_evidence.py --require-pass. LIMITS OF WHAT WAS MEASURED: `retail` is read access to original files and byte inspection of the owner-supplied decrypted executable is static analysis — neither is a run of the original; which world axis each stored eye component is, and the unit conversion into this project's right/up/forward body frame, is unrecorded (the triple is carried in the archive's source units); what the two dispatched camera modes are called in the original UI is unrecorded; the `cocky`/`cockz` script override channel is measured but the values a script writes are runtime state; whether the original's traversal-order tiebreak is ever needed is unrecorded because no retail airframe stores two matching nodes. `claim` is `implemented` only. `candidate_tree` is the tree of the commit the suite ran on; the only later delta is this report's own copy under docs/findings/evidence/, whose bytes are that file.
